thread.title: Apple Pay Adds Taco Bell, Target, Speedway | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Pay Adds Taco Bell, Target, Speedway | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) goal to turn the iPhone into a digital wallet is gaining steam as the company announced Tuesday that Apple Pay is now supported by 65% of all retail locations across the U.S.
X Target ( TGT ), Taco Bell, Jack in the Box ( JACK ), Speedway convenience stores and Hy-Vee supermarkets are the latest merchants to support Apple's mobile contactless payment system. With the addition of those retailers, 74 of the top 100 merchants in the U.S. now accept Apple Pay, the company said in a news release .
"Whether customers are buying everyday household items, groceries, snacks for a road trip or grabbing a quick meal, Apple Pay is the easiest way to pay in stores, while also being secure and faster than using a credit or debit card at the register," Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Internet Services, said in a written statement.
Customers can use Apple Pay now at more than 245 Hy-Vee stores in the Midwest and inside the store at all of Speedway's roughly 3,000 locations across the Midwest, East Coast and Southeast.

Plus, all 1,850 Target stores across the country will install the payment service in the coming weeks, Apple said.
Last year, 7-Eleven launched Apple Pay at 95% of its U.S. stores. Costco ( COST ) completed the rollout of Apple Pay to over 500 U.S. warehouses. CVS Pharmacy introduced Apple Pay at all of its nearly 8,400 stand-alone locations.
Apple's payment service works on the Apple Watch as well as the iPhone.
Apple shares fell 2.2% to 153.30 on the stock market today .
